story.title: I Built Non-Autoregressive Decision Models with RL a Year Ago

draft:
I proved you can skip the token‑by‑token grind and still let a model learn to act.

A year ago I built a non‑autoregressive decision model trained with reinforcement learning. Instead of generating one step after another, the network predicts the entire action set in parallel and receives a single reward signal. The result was a 3‑5× speedup on benchmark tasks with only a modest drop in optimality.

What surprised me most wasn’t the raw latency gain—it was how the RL signal forced the model to discover coordinated strategies that a classic autoregressive decoder would never explore. The trade‑off between parallelism and precision feels like a new design knob for any system where decisions must be made under tight time constraints.

I’m curious: which real‑world pipelines could tolerate a little “wiggle room” in exchange for massive throughput?
